implementations.name: parameterized modular lagged difference
implementations.difference: Every profile applies the same update independently to each semantic input stream: residual[i]=current[i]-history[lag] in that stream, then the inverse adds the same history value. implementations.name: parameterized C-Blosc2 BLOSCLZ-5 with byte shuffle
implementations.difference: After removing the surrounding exact-stage adapters, both entries run the same C-Blosc2 pipeline: BLOSCLZ, compression level 5, byte shuffle, one thread, automatic block size, forward-compatible split mode, and no delta filter. P114 uses the context API; P119 uses the legacy global API, which builds the same filter list and initializes the same compression context. A direct v3.1.5-to-v3.3.3 source comparison shows that the byte-shuffle sources are identical, the blosc2.c differences do not touch this compression pipeline, and the BLOSCLZ compressor changes only rewrite output-bound checks into overflow-safe algebraically equivalent forms; the match parser, entropy probe, hash update, and token emission are unchanged. P114 first decodes the project Blosc prefix, while P119 converts the returned chunk to B2P1; those are input/output adapters, and the B2P1 operation is already represented independently by P127. The linked C-Blosc2 release and typesize are execution profiles and must be pinned for reproducible builds, but they do not define another operator algorithm under the requested equivalence rule.
parameters_or_profiles: typesize: P114 accepts 1, 4, or 8; P119 currently fixes 1
linked C-Blosc2 release: P114 vendored 3.1.5.dev; P119 requires 3.3.3
input adapter: P114 reverses the project Blosc prefix before the backend call
output adapter: P119 converts the native chunk to the B2P1 logical-block packet represented by P127
environment/global settings must be frozen: compressor=BLOSCLZ, clevel=5, shuffle, delta=0, blocksize=auto, split=forward-compatible, nthreads=1
